evidence.claim: Case-memory scorer (calibrated on the bank's closed cases) scores the flagged transaction 3514948 at cms_p=0.8491 (cal_p 0.7674), essentially matching the real-time risk_score of 0.87.

A second in-person transaction in the same 48h window, 3514573 ($36.97, region 264.0, 2016-12-04 22:40:36), scores cms_p=0.72, standing out from the surrounding baseline of sub-0.03 cms_p values on this card.

Card C09933-K2 has 18 prior confirmed-fraud closed cases (pattern account_takeover / out_of_region_use, template fraud_reported), the most recent CC-5521 closed 2016-10-31 for $730.52 across 9 transactions.

8 of this card's prior confirmed-fraud cases were labeled account_takeover and confirmed inside the card's own modal region, so an in-region purchase does not rule out fraud on this card -- it is this card's established fraud shape.
The flagged amount, $111.92, sits inside the card's baseline: prior median $77.04 and prior maximum $2,529.78 over 2,431 prior in-region transactions.

Region 264.0 is the card's modal in-person region: 2,224 prior purchases over 156 days, 91.9% share of all activity, with home activity continuing through the 48h window (24 home vs 2 other transactions).

The flagged amount recurs at this billing region: 5 prior product-W purchases within +-1% of $111.92 at region 264.0, median gap 16.0 days but gap CV 0.60, so it narrowly misses R7's monthly-recurrence gate.

One prior risk-score alert on this card was cleared after customer confirmation (CC-0657, 2016-07-17, exposure $0), but it was a different (amount) shape, making it a weak legitimacy precedent against 18 confirmed frauds.
Assumed reply: no reply from the customer within 24 hours

case.summary: This risk-score alert on card C09933-K2 (txn 3514948, $111.92, in-person, region 264.0) closes as verdict fraud at probability 0.77, pattern account_takeover: an all-in-person episode inside the card's own modal region. The episode is 3508487 ($116.96, 2016-12-02), 3514573 ($36.97, 2016-12-04) and 3514948 ($111.92, 2016-12-05), all scoring sharply above the card's baseline cms_p (0.85, 0.72 and 0.85 versus a sea of sub-0.03 values in the same window), for exposure $265.85. The decisive family was case memory: this exact card carries 18 confirmed-fraud closed cases in this same account_takeover/out_of_region_use shape, most recently closed 2016-10-31, so a high-cms_p purchase here is this card's established fraud pattern rather than reassuring "home region" activity; the history family (amount within baseline, modal region, a loosely recurring ~$110 price point) pulled the other way, which is the alternative reading -- several same-region alerts on this card's neighborhood were in fact cleared as legitimate (e.g. CC-4591, CC-5008, CC-3761, CC-5401), so a benign in-person purchase at a familiar merchant cannot be ruled out from the graph alone. A customer_validation request was sent to settle the conflict; no reply arrived within the 24-hour window, so per R4 the assumption is no_reply and the case proceeds on the fraud-band recommendation. The bank should CREATE_CASE (auto), MONITOR_CARD (auto) and DECLINE_TRANSACTION (L1) for any pending authorizations, and BLOCK_CARD (L1, exposure $265.85 ≤ $2,500); BLOCK_ALL_CARDS stays forbidden under R10 since only this one card shows the fraud signal, and no SAR is filed because exposure is under $1,000 and there is no shared device or region cluster.
